John —

Great speaking with you. Looping in Dev and Neha from our security/engineering team to provide the technical summary below. Quick recap and proposed next steps:

1) Redwood Hosted (default): we do not persist full request/response bodies by default for customer workloads. We offer configurable request/response logging for debugging; when enabled it can be scoped to specific routes and time windows.
2) Redaction: masking can be applied at ingest (regex or structured-key redaction) and at storage (tokenization/hashing). We can also automatically strip common PII fields (emails, SSNs, credit-card-like patterns) via our redaction engine.
3) Retention: default debug logs are retained for 30 days; audit logs (route/access events, model version used, latency metrics) can be retained longer (90/365 days) depending on plan and region. Dedicated/Private deployments give you control to set retention to meet policy.

Next steps:
- Dev/security to confirm specifics on headers/trace IDs and provide an example policy snippet.
- I’ll share the SOC2-evidence-summary.pdf and an excerpt of our logging policy.

If you’re comfortable, we can schedule a quick 30-minute tech deep-dive next week for compliance.

Best,

John / Marissa —

Below is a concise technical summary addressing the specific questions from the call and the attached redaction spreadsheet. I tried to map items to Hosted / Dedicated / Private where relevant.

1) What is logged by default (Hosted):
   - Request metadata: timestamp, route, model ID, model version, token counts, latency, outcome (success/error).
   - Request/response bodies: NOT persisted by default. We capture request/response bodies only when customer enables debug logging for specific routes.
   - Headers: we persist non-sensitive routing headers (e.g., region, content-type). Authorization headers and any header matching configured sensitive keys are masked/omitted.

2) Trace IDs and observability:
   - We include a generated trace_id for each request and surface it in metrics and audit logs. By default the trace_id is retained without associated full payloads. If you enable request/response logging, trace_id will be present in those logs for correlation.
   - If you require retention of trace IDs but not bodies, we can provide a policy that stores only trace_id + metadata for X days (configurable).

3) Redaction/masking options:
   - Ingest-time redaction: regex-based and schema-aware redactors that can strip or replace configured keys (e.g., "email", "ssn", "card_number"). Patterns from your spreadsheet can be onboarded as custom rules.
   - Post-ingest tokenization: sensitive values can be replaced with stable tokens/hashes (useful for correlation while keeping raw PII out of logs).
   - Header masking: configure a header allowlist; everything else is redacted or not stored.
   - Response-side masking: for structured outputs (JSON), Redwood can apply output filters to ensure model responses do not include PII before they're logged or returned to storage.

4) Retention windows and export:
   - Hosted default: debug bodies 30 days; audit logs 90 days.
   - Dedicated/Private: retention windows are configurable; many customers set debug bodies to 7/14/30 days and audit logs to 365 days for compliance.
   - All logs can be exported to your S3/GCS bucket daily for long-term storage under your control (we support signed transfer and KMS integration).

5) Security controls & evidence:
   - SOC2 artifacts: we can share the SOC2-evidence-summary.pdf (attached) and schedule an encrypted artifact transfer if you need deeper evidence.
   - Key management: in Private and Dedicated, you can bring-your-own-KMS; hosted offers managed KMS with customer-specific access controls.

6) Custom rule example (from your spreadsheet):
   - Field: "user.email" -> action: mask (retain domain only)
   - Field: "payment.card_number" -> action: tokenize + store only last4

Caveats / notes:
   - Debug logging is intended for short windows to debug incidents; we recommend using tokenization or schema-aware redaction if you need long-term correlatable data without raw PII.
   - For regulated workloads we recommend Private or Dedicated with retention policies set and logs exported to your controlled storage.

If helpful I can paste an example policy snippet and a short JSON sample showing pre/post-redaction. Would you like that included here or in the tech deep-dive?
